description: Table 3 is a rendered data table (no axes, curves or images) titled "Vickers hardness values of the 17Al alloys after different aging treatments". Rows are aging temperatures — 525 °C, 550 °C aging, 575 °C aging, 600 °C aging, 625 °C aging and 650 °C aging — and columns are aging times — Solution-treated, 1 h, 3 h, 6 h, 10 h. Every cell contains a Vickers hardness in HV with a ± standard deviation. The solution-treated value 259.8 ± 1.5 HV is printed once and spans all rows via a merged cell. Hardness rises strongly with aging at every temperature. At 525 °C it increases monotonically from 566.9 ± 9.7 HV (1 h) to 616.8 ± 12.3 HV (10 h). At 575 °C hardness climbs from 438.1 ± 39.3 HV (1 h) to a table maximum of 924.9 ± 25.8 HV at 6 h, then drops to 831.3 ± 27.4 HV at 10 h. The 625 °C and 650 °C rows reach ~813–878 HV and ~828–838 HV respectively and stay nearly flat across 1–10 h. The table shows that a 575 °C / 6 h aging window maximizes hardness of the 17Al alloy, while all aged conditions far exceed the solution-treated baseline.

Twelve+ hardness cells, each a mean ± standard deviation in HV; values range from 438.1 ± 39.3 HV (575 °C, 1 h) to 924.9 ± 25.8 HV (575 °C, 6 h), the highest entry in the table.

observations.observation: Table 3 lists Vickers hardness (HV) of the 17Al alloys after aging at 525 °C, 550 °C, 575 °C, 600 °C, 625 °C and 650 °C for 1 h, 3 h, 6 h and 10 h.
The solution-treated value is given once as 259.8 ± 1.5 HV and spans all aging-temperature rows (merged cell in the 'Solution-treated' column).
All aged hardness values (438.1 HV to 924.9 HV) are far above the solution-treated baseline of 259.8 ± 1.5 HV.
At 525 °C hardness rises monotonically with time: 566.9 ± 9.7 HV (1 h), 585.0 ± 6.1 HV (3 h), 598.9 ± 10.4 HV (6 h), 616.8 ± 12.3 HV (10 h).
At 575 °C hardness increases from 438.1 ± 39.3 HV (1 h) to 811.7 ± 39.3 HV (3 h) to the table maximum 924.9 ± 25.8 HV (6 h), then decreases to 831.3 ± 27.4 HV (10 h).
The highest hardness printed in Table 3 is 924.9 ± 25.8 HV, for the 575 °C / 6 h aging condition.
The 600 °C row starts high at 862.7 ± 28.0 HV (1 h), dips to 794.6 ± 58.1 HV at 3 h, then recovers to 840.4 ± 18.5 HV (6 h) and 837.3 ± 15.3 HV (10 h).
The 625 °C row is nearly flat across time: 813.0 ± 20.8, 872.0 ± 24.4, 878.4 ± 28.3 and 870.5 ± 24.9 HV for 1, 3, 6 and 10 h.
The 650 °C row is the flattest, varying only between 828.4 ± 26.6 HV (1 h) and 838.3 ± 20.7 HV (6 h).
The largest scatter reported is ±58.1 HV for the 600 °C / 3 h condition; most other uncertainties are between about ±6 and ±39 HV.

At short aging (1 h) hardness increases with aging temperature, from 566.9 ± 9.7 HV at 525 °C to 862.7 ± 28.0 HV at 600 °C, whereas at 10 h the 575-650 °C values all fall in a narrow band of about 831-870 HV.
The caption states the table reports Vickers hardness values of the 17Al alloys after different aging treatments.
